title: Naturality of descended componentwise tensor-Hom uncurrying
statement: Let t be any family of derived tensor-Hom functions for a scheme X. Assume its values on all K-flat chain representatives are the localization of the explicit coproduct uncurrying map of [lem-pc-tensor-hom-uncurry-differential], and that t is compatible with all isomorphisms in the three derived variables. Then t is natural for arbitrary derived morphisms a:Kprime -> K, b:Lprime -> L, c:M -> Mprime: t(a followed by f followed by RHom(b,c)) equals (a tensor b) followed by t(f) followed by c. This is a conditional theorem about an arbitrary family, not an existence statement.

source.place: Tag 08DJ; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 0A90 and 0A96; online source consulted at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08DJ and /tag/0A90

proof.text: Apply lem-pc-tensor-hom-uncurry-chain-naturality to obtain simultaneous naturality for Q-images of actual chain maps, with arbitrary derived input f. This retains the componentwise evaluation calculation and K-flat/K-injective route of the original proof.

For each of a, b, c separately, choose source and target complex representatives using essential surjectivity of Q. Conjugate the arrow by the endpoint isomorphisms and apply Mathlib DerivedCategory.right_fac, the cochain specialization of right-fraction representation. If the conjugated arrow is inv(Qs) followed by Qg, absorb the invertible Qs into the source endpoint isomorphism. This produces a chain map and two endpoint isomorphisms with commuting arrow square. No chosen complex is defined from a holed existence theorem: the representatives and fractions are local witnesses in a proof.

Transport f to the source representatives by eK.hom followed by f followed by RHom(eL.hom,eM.inv). The arrow squares and the functor map_comp law show that pre/postcomposing this input by the three chain maps equals transporting the original transformed input. Apply chain-map naturality, then apply hi once to the source value and once to the target value. The tensor interchange law identifies the two tensor composites. Cancel the tensor of the source endpoint isomorphisms on the left and the target endpoint inverse on the right. This gives precisely the asserted equality for arbitrary a,b,c. This is the private naturality_transport proof; it uses no linearity or bijectivity of t.
